SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-15, form: pools per market over a consignment). PRODUCTION.md § Stockpile and output flow owns it; MARKETS.md § Market centres and seeding and SUPPLY.md § Convoy entity amended.

items.title: The CTest tier links what its harnesses now use: a family of Debug targets has been unbuildable since the harnesses adopted the app-order build
items.design:
FOUND 2026-09-22 running BL-1044's owed ctest pass. `nmake all` stops at the first failing target, so the suite reads as "Not Run" rather than as a broken build, and the breakage hid.

WHAT IS BROKEN. Every harness that builds its world in APP ORDER goes through tools/verify/harness_params.hpp, which includes scripting/lua_state.hpp and calls build_app_base_world — so it needs lua54 AND the Lua TUs the Lua-free world superset excludes (world_gen_config.cpp, works_registry.cpp, recipe_registry.cpp, tech_tree.cpp). The CMake targets name those by hand, one target at a time, and the ones written before harness_params spread do not. Measured tonight, building all 157 CTest targets by name: player_seed_sweep failed on LNK2019 world_gen_config::load_from_lua / works_registry::load_from_lua (fixed at ee7ef3c3, which restored the player_seed_sweep_guard row — the row that now carries the one-player invariant, S7); campaign_lapse, chain_conversion_probe, convoy_cargo_census and others fail on LNK2019 lua_close / luaL_unref, i.e. they do not link lua54 at all. battle_engagement_harness is a separate, older break (a torn-out mercenary symbol, 2026-08-30).

THE WORK. Take the failing list from the overnight build (scratchpad overnight3/build_failures.txt, or rebuild by name to regenerate it); for each, add lua54 and whichever Lua TUs it pulls, or move it onto a shared helper so the list stops being hand-kept — the hand-kept list is the defect, and DEVELOPMENT_PRACTICES.md § A harness must build the world the application builds is what keeps growing it. Then run the suite and record which rows breach the 60 s default now that the span runs by default (BL-1044: the budget row's generation is a median 53.3 s in Release).

DONE WHEN. Every CTest target builds by name, `ctest --test-dir build` runs every row rather than reporting Not Run, and the rows that legitimately exceed 60 s carry a raised timeout with the reason.

THE LIST, measured 2026-09-22 by building all 157 CTest test names (14 stops, three classes). (a) DOES NOT LINK LUA (LNK2019 lua_close / luaL_unref), 9: campaign_lapse, chain_conversion_probe, convoy_cargo_census, industrialisation_sim_harness, exploration_sweep, history_sweep, material_floor, stockpile_budget_check, world_copy_determinism. (b) DOES NOT COMPILE against the current headers, 3: whole_firm_buyout and battle_engagement_harness read world::mercenary_contracts, retired by NR-885 on 2026-09-17; nation_scorer_harness fails on a missing type. Those are stale harnesses, not a link list — each is a decision to re-point or retire. (c) NOT A TARGET, 1: player_seed_sweep_guard is a ctest TEST name whose target is player_seed_sweep (fixed at ee7ef3c3); the build loop took test names, so a name that is not a target reads as a stop.

items.author: Claude (found running BL-1044's owed visual suite, 2026-09-23)
items.title: The player's own construction does not complete on the shipped world: a military base sits unfinished for 100 ticks with 70,000 credits in hand
items.design:
DIAGNOSED 2026-09-23 (Release --verify probes with a temporary run_construction trace; probes and patch in that session's scratchpad). Capacity is NOT the stall: BL-709 floors capacity coverage at 1/max_stretch, so it only stretches. The stall is MATERIALS, in three layers:

(1) WRONG MARKET, AND NOTHING CAN REFILL IT. The fixture's build_first_valid placed at raster-first tile (45,97), market 56211: 0 steel for 100 ticks, demand there 0.00 — the build's want booked at the corp's representative market, not the draw market. Steel existed on the body (558 units) but in 5 of 255 markets, and a same-body convoy lands in the seller's own (corp, body) pool. Structural cause, owned by BL-1003 (pools per market).

(2) THE SITE MULTIPLIER DRAWS MORE THAN WAS PRICED. The per-tick draw is cost/build_duration_ticks per unit of progress, but ticks_remaining carries BL-323's site multiplier, so a hard site draws cost x multiplier while construct_building's affordability gate priced the authored cost. Placed next to home (market 56166, 36.5 steel), the 35-steel base drew 36.5, stalled at 4.1 of 5+ progress units and never finished.

(3) ZERO CONSTRUCTION CAPACITY. 0 construction yards on the body, so every build runs at the 10% floor: a 4-tick base takes 40+ ticks (ten years at a quarterly tick).

RULINGS (Ben, 2026-09-23, form):
- Sourcing: restore BL-1003 (pools per market). This item requires it.
- Site multiplier: it stretches MATERIALS AND CASH as well as time, and that is PRICED AT PLACEMENT — the affordability gate, the Build door's capex preview and the rival scorer price cost x the site multiplier (PRODUCTION.md § Construction site time).
- Capacity: IN SCOPE here. Either the charter web charters a yard the player's catchment reaches, or the opening corp carries capacity; choose by measurement once BL-1003 has landed, since pools per market move where capacity sits.

PLUS THE FIXTURE: scripts/verify/lib.lua must place near the player's own works (not raster-first) and wait out the 12-tick tech gate, and its error must say 'stalled' when progress stops rather than 'never completed within 40 ticks'.

DONE WHEN. On every library seed, the seated player can place AND complete a military base in its home catchment within the fixture's bound; the affordability gate refuses a site whose multiplied cost the corp cannot meet; and scripts/verify/lib.lua stages on a pristine world.

ROUND 2 (2026-09-23, after BL-1003 merged; traces in that session scratchpad). With pools per market the build want reaches its own market (demand 8.75, steel priced 161) and convoys dispatch, but the base still stalled: (i) ~3,000 steel, nearly all the body pooled, sat in NINE BL-910 capital markets with base price 0 — never listed; (ii) the shortfall dispatcher ran at the top of the tick and credited arrivals at its end, so every delivery was re-exported before any clearing saw it (995 steel dispatches in 100 ticks into one market); (iii) with capacity stocked by hand the base ran at full rate and then starved for steel, so capacity is necessary but not sufficient.

RULINGS (Ben, 2026-09-23): capital markets are PRICED, at a premium over the carve (MARKETS.md; the size is NR-916) — this absorbs the sprint 46 draft CAPITAL_MARKET_SHELLS, whose census-then-choose plan the ruling replaces; and the tick order is advance -> arrivals -> economy -> clearing -> dispatch (SUPPLY.md § Dispatch trigger, one beat per haul). The goods-vs-force LP priority that reorder flips is NR-917.

ROUND 3 (2026-09-23, after BL-995 merged f274a3d5). Trade is now real world-wide (haulage_measure --far-trade, 4 seeds: 3,712 units sold at destinations in year one, 82.5% of it past the seller’s nearest market). The base still stalls, and the trace says why: STEEL PRODUCTION ON THE BODY COLLAPSES — listed steel 234/tick at tick 1, 75 by tick 5, 0 from ~tick 9 in every market — while unmet steel demand climbs 0 -> 341/tick; and the ~3,460 steel of opening stock was sold to the SHELVES at tick 1 (before any price gap existed), where it belongs to no one and never moves. With capacity stocked by hand the base runs at full rate and starves the moment its local shelf empties. Open: (1) why the shipped world stops making steel within ~9 ticks; (2) whether shelf stock should ever move (a merchant buying low and hauling — the option passed over for BL-995); (3) construction capacity, a TRANSMITTED good (road network, like power), so its reach is a wiring question — the earlier '0 yards' reading was a probe miscount by type name.

WORLD RULED (Ben, 2026-09-24, option B): BL-1066's done-when is taken on the FLIPPED world — after BL-1047 (epoch flip gates), on the 1960 world the player is actually handed — not on the epoch-0 verify world every reading so far was taken on (steel_chain_probe found epoch 0 is the ancient band with no steel makers at all; its anachronisms are BL-1070). Epoch 0 stays a supported start (Ben, same day).

CARRIED 2026-09-24: sprint 46 closed early; unscheduled pending the sprint 47 cut.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-24: goods should move); Claude
items.title: Stock on a market's shelf can move to a better market; today it belongs to no one and never leaves
items.design:
MECHANISM RULED (Ben, 2026-09-24): option (b) — the market exports its own surplus shelf stock by the net-price rule, the haul paid from the export. SUPPLY.md § Dispatch trigger ('A market exports its own shelf') owns it.

THE WORK. In the dispatch step, AFTER corporations' dispatch: for each market and good, shelf inventory (above what its own local consumers drew last clear — measure, do not guess) is a source under net(d) = price_d - haul - [handling, duty when built]; send to argmax net(d) above the margin, quantity = the same absorbable room corporations use (all pending subtracted). The convoy has no corporation: model its owner as the source market (a convoy field or a sentinel owner) and settle: on arrival the cargo lands on the DESTINATION market's shelf and sells there; the haul is charged against the export's proceeds — decide with FINANCE.md where the net proceeds go (the source market holds no treasury today: the options are that they vanish as the market's margin, or credit the source market's nation as a tariff-like line) and state it. Interdiction, LP and the arrived-this-tick rule apply as to any convoy. Harness rows: a shelf with a far better-priced market exports; one under the margin does not; no churn; goods conserved (shelf debit = cargo = destination shelf credit).

DONE WHEN. On the epoch-0 verify world the stranded shelf steel moves toward the markets pricing it (steel_chain_probe's shelf geography), and haulage_measure --far-trade shows market exports as their own line.

--- EARLIER ---
RULED IN DIRECTION (Ben, 2026-09-24: 'goods should move'); the MECHANISM is open. FOUND on BL-1066: auto-surplus sells every unit above processor reservation to the local market (the market is buyer of last resort), and market inventory has no owner, so nothing hauls it — on the epoch-0 verify world ~3,300 steel sat on 13 of 255 shelves while construction sites elsewhere paused for it. BL-995 (trade reaches for price) makes a SELLER haul before it sells; stock already on a shelf still cannot move.

MECHANISM OPTIONS (Ben's call, then written into SUPPLY.md and MARKETS.md): (a) any corporation may BUY shelf stock at the shelf's price and haul it under the same net-price rule — a merchant is just a corp acting on a gap, one rule for every corp; (b) the market itself exports its surplus shelf stock by the net-price rule, the haul paid from the sale; (c) a construction site or processor may buy from the nearest stocked shelf across markets, paying the haul (narrow: fixes consumers, not trade).

DONE WHEN. A shelf holding a good that another market prices above landed cost is drawn down by hauls, measured by haulage_measure --far-trade and steel_chain_probe's shelf geography.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-24, the sprint 47 design form); Claude
items.title: The world is built once at the Life gate, with its deposits, and moves forward through every wizard round instead of being rebuilt
items.design:
SPRINT 48 CUT (Ben, 2026-09-25, the cut form): NEXT WAITS (NR-936 closed). The wizard's Next is disabled while the round on screen is running and enables the moment its world lands; its hover names what it waits on (STARTUP.md § The wait, then the lapse). So no two pass rounds build at once and the peak NR-936 observed cannot occur. The done-when's first clause reads under it: Next on round 4 is live only once round 4 has landed, round 5's wait caption names only the Exploration span, and its elapsed count is the Exploration span's own cost.

CARRIED TO SPRINT 48 (Ben, 2026-09-25, the sprint-47 close form): sprint 47 closes on the identity wave and its flair; this item opens sprint 48. NR-936 rides with it: the wizard's Next press does not wait for the running round, so a fast player can have rounds 3-6 building at once; with one world moved forward, round N+1 cannot start before round N lands, so decide here whether Next waits.

RULED (Ben, 2026-09-24: "move the whole half-built world"; "we don't want to do the work twice, so seed actual materials at the Life gate and pass tiles through the whole phase"; docs/development/drafts/sprint-47-rulings.md R1, R2).

WHY. Every lapse round's worker runs make_hard_coded_world from params to its own stop (startup_screens.cpp:375-379): stages 0-7 (Helios, Cinder, the Kepler chain, tiles with deposits, rivers, creeds, settlement) run again on every seam, and round 5 re-runs Empires, round 6 re-runs Empires and Exploration (hard_coded_world.cpp:550-916, :1158, :1313, :1497). Rounds 0-1 build a scratch world for the globe and discard it. Deposits already land at stage 4 (tile_generation.cpp Pass 6, generate_life_deposits_over :2284-2298), downstream of S8 Legacy and S9 Spend (planetology.cpp:1533-1555), so the ruling changes OWNERSHIP, not pass order.

THE WORK. (1) make_hard_coded_world becomes the composition of resumable stage functions over one generation_cursor carrying what the tail reads as locals today (world, report, naming, rw, deposit_scalar, kepler_tiles/pl/hist/creeds/settlement/np/corridors/grudges/region_polity/polity_treasuries/capital_market_shells, the last span's resume struct): gen_life_gate (bumps 0-5), gen_culture (:826-1138), gen_empires (:1158-1300), gen_exploration (:1313-1470), gen_industrialisation (:1488-1640) then the tail (bumps 9-12). The composition is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the monolith: every harness, fixture, gen_step_costs and the 16 seed-library pins keep one invocation. The stop_after_* flags stop being early returns and become 'run the composition up to stage N'. (2) The wizard: the Life round builds the REAL Life-gate world into slot 0 (the globe rasters pack off it; a planetology move relaunches it and drops every slot below); launch_wizard_history_run(i) takes slot i-1 and runs only stage i into slot i; invalidate_wizard_rounds_below(r) drops every slot below r and stale-marks in-flight ones (a stale landing drops record AND world, the pattern at startup_screens.cpp:439-449); Begin adopts slot 3 exactly as BL-1073 does. (3) The reroll path (delegated reading, NEEDS_REVIEW): the predecessor's closed world is HELD by a faithful copy at landing (BL-1034; world_copy_determinism proves a copy ticks as its original) and a copy is moved into the worker; a reroll re-copies; when the predecessor is not held, REPLAY from the Life gate with the fixed per-span seeds — bit-identical by determinism, ~0.5 s + 1.6 s + 1.5 s in Release (hard_coded_world.cpp:360-398). Measure the copy cost first (Rule 0b); if it exceeds the replay it saves, ship pure replay. Back keeps every record and world. (4) The gate world is Helios + Cinder + Kepler; Selene and Pallas stay in Finishing (an entity-id shift for two bodies no round shows — NEEDS_REVIEW). (5) Round 6 starts playing at the tap's final publish (history_sim.cpp:7899; the record is whole there); landing only swaps the world slot; poll_wizard_history_tap's snapshot path and the landed path must not fight over m_wiz_history[3]. (6) Proof: world_determinism twice; a cursor-vs-monolith check (owner_changes, polities, world digest) at EVERY round boundary on the 16 curated seeds, extending run_autostart_adopt's round-6 proof; begin_adopts_check.js green.

DONE WHEN (live). Press Next on rounds 4 and 5: the wait caption never names an earlier span ('Running the ancient era' never appears on round 5) and the elapsed count is shorter by the predecessor's measured cost; Back then Next on any round recomputes nothing; reroll round 5 and it opens on round 4's exact 1200 frame. Harness: the resumed build equals the monolithic build on the 16 seeds; digests unchanged.

items.author: Ben (2026-09-25, the sprint 48 cut form's notes); filed by Claude
items.title: A market can be destroyed, so the world handed to the player never carries too many markets
items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-10-03): the port gate stands (a fold crosses water only where both cities' regions hold a port, as a convoy needs) and the reach is 16 (15 of 16 seeds in 20-40).

RULED (Ben, 2026-10-03): haulage halving accepted pending a re-read after BL-1138; keep 20-40 and drop the per-city phrasing; capitals fold like any market.

SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-25, the density form): three causes destroy a market, written into MARKETS.md § Market centres and seeding. (1) TWINS FOLD: a market centred on the same tile as another folds into the lower-id one. (2) GRAVITY FOLD: a market inside a larger market's reach (traversal cost) folds into it; larger = catchment population; the reach constant is CALIBRATED so a 1960 world carries roughly 20-40 markets, about one per major city (Ben picked "20-40, a market per major city" over the recommended 50-100) -- an aim for the constant measured on the curated seeds, never a count the rule enforces. (3) CONQUEST CONSOLIDATES (Ben's note: "when an empire conquers territory, it would destroy the market to consolidate strength"): conquering the region a rival's market stands on destroys that market. Not chosen: capital death as a separate rule (conquest covers the dead-maker case), the junction tightened, a runtime death in play. A folded market's catchment, inventory and pools pass to its absorber.

SEQUENCE. BL-1130 (centres consolidate) lands first: the carve follows centre density, so the gravity constant is calibrated on the consolidated world, not today's. Conquest is history-grain (history_sim.cpp, where region::has_market is marked at each span close) and independent of the carve, so it can run beside BL-1130. The twins fold and the gravity fold run at the carve, after the junction rule, on the whole set.

CENSUS READ 2026-09-25 (market_census, 16 curated seeds, the handed-over 1960 world; tools/verify/market_census.cpp). 4,984 markets, 311.5 a seed (148-538; seed 0's 255 is ordinary). By source: capital shells 1,246 (25%), carve 3,738 (75%), of which 2,532 (68% of the carve) exist only because the junction rule lowered the gate. Shells are marked at EVERY span close, not only 1200 (1,168 at 1200, 68 at 1660, 10 at 1960; the mark is sticky); at 1960 the maker still holds 829, holds its capital elsewhere 98, is dead 319 -- 417 lost, 392 of them standing on no living capital. TWINS: 1,043 markets (21%) are centred on the same tile as a lower-id market and can never win a tile (market_for_tile breaks ties to the lowest id): 826 carve under carve, 217 carve under a shell. Catchment median 15 tiles (carve 9, shells 100); nearest other market centre median 1.0 tile (0.4 traversal cost). 4,442 of 4,984 have no building in their catchment at the handoff; 3,523 (71%) clear nothing across the first play year (shells 41%, carve 81%). The count is the carve, and the carve follows population-centre density (the roads lane found centres on 49-100% of land). Also found and filed: BL-1127 (market_for_tile ignores the column wrap, 3.1% of tiles misroute).

FILED 2026-09-25 (Ben, the sprint 48 cut form's notes: "We should also work on making sure markets can be destroyed, so that the end result never has too many markets"). In sprint 48. The intent is ruled; the mechanism is Ben's, against a census.

WHAT STANDS TODAY. MARKETS.md says a market never disappears: nothing removes an entry from world::markets, the BL-768 junction rule only ever lowers the gate, and an idle off-world market goes dormant. The home body's markets come from two sources: a shell at the capital of every polity alive at the 1200 close (history_sim.cpp ~8262-8281 marks region::has_market at every span close, not only 1200; hard_coded_world.cpp ~1882-1915 spawns it; the capital premium prices it, ~2695-2716), and the carve over population centres (~2574-2617). Nothing after 1200 un-marks a capital that fell in a later span. BL-1003's reading (2026-09-23) found 255 markets on the shipped home body; MARKETS.md § Market centres still says nine on seed 0.

THE WORK, measure first (Rule 0b). (1) A census per curated seed on the flipped 1960 world: markets by source (capital shell, carve, junction-lowered), how many shells stand where the polity died after 1200, catchment tiles and population per market, and the share that clear nothing in the first play year. Built as a committed harness, not a probe. (2) Ben rules the mechanism against it. Candidates, not exclusive: a capital's market dies with its capital unless the carve would place one there; a market inside a larger one's reach folds into it (a gravity rule over traversal cost); a runtime death for a market that clears nothing for a span, which moves save format, per-market pools, convoys, standing orders and trades onto a successor. Whatever the rule, it is an in-world cause a player could read, never a count cap. (3) Build it, write the rule into MARKETS.md (retiring "a market never disappears" wherever it stops holding), and correct the stale nine.

A WORLD-MOVER: a named cause in the sprint's one re-bless.

DONE WHEN. The census is committed and recorded per seed; the ruled mechanism runs; the 1960 market count per seed is recorded old -> new; MARKETS.md states the rule; every harness that reads markets is green.

items.title: Villages consolidate into towns as a region grows, and no region carries more centres than its ground holds
items.design:
ROUND 2 READING RULED (Ben, 2026-09-25): the campaign prize (campaign_prize_q's centres x 200) and the reach relay (150 per centre, capped 500) READ URBAN HEADS, calibrated so the same heads give the same value as the old centre count did (POPULATION.md: a place's size is its people). Round 3 builds it; then merge. CORRECTION (2026-09-25): the re-settlement gate (a region re-settles only after a recorded razing) was judged a legitimate consequence by the lane, not ruled by Ben; round 3 measured that it moves the history substantially on its own, and with the sub-village floor it is put to Ben (the settlement-value form). ROUND 3 (c2548e1b): the heads mapping (min(heads/10,000, 32)) reproduces main for 91-94% of Empires-span prize/relay evaluations; the rest is the floor (main valued every settled region at one centre even under 10k heads) and a freeze class; synthetic R1 180 battles (main 7); floor candidate + the gate at main's reading reproduces main exactly on seed 40 (R1 8). Census: centres 164,982 -> 66,867, land 70.4% -> 28.5%.

SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-25, the open-calls form at the live app): EXPLAIN FIRST, THEN MERGE -- find why the history moved (a synthetic run's battles 7 -> 98; seed 40's regions 1,461 -> 2,703; candidates: campaign_prize_q's centres x 200 term, the relay rule centres >= relay_min) before the branch merges. Keep the per-region size hierarchy; a region whose cell holds no land carries NO centre (POPULATION.md). Follow-ons this sprint: BL-1132 (settle spacing), BL-1133 (anchors reuse a centre), BL-1137 (industrial urbanisation, the "dramatically fewer" lever), with the market folds (BL-1125) calibrated after them.

SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-25, the density form) (POPULATION.md § Generation, "Growth consolidates"). FOUND BY THE ROADS LANE (BL-1119 D1, 2026-09-25): population centres cover 49-100% of land on the 16 curated seeds (seed 46: 15,240 centres on 15,240 land tiles), every centre is a street, so the "lattice" Ben saw is streets and no road rule can thin it; the carve markets (75% of ~311 a world, BL-1125's census) follow the same density. POPULATION.md already wants "a few cities over many towns over a train of villages" and records that the remaining displacements are regions "wanting more cities than it has ground".

THE RULE. As a region's urban heads rise, its villages merge into a town rather than a new village standing beside them; a region never carries more centres than its ground holds (their urban footprints fit inside its own cell); a built-out cell promotes a centre it already has instead of spilling one into a neighbour's cell. Pure integer functions of the region record, no RNG, as the rest of the demography.

THE WORK, measure first (Rule 0b). (1) Read where the region's `centres` integer grows (the history's urban growth and promotion) and where generate_population_centres spills; report centres per seed, land share covered by centres, scale distribution, spills -- old. (2) Build the rule. (3) Report the same -- new -- plus the carve's market count (market_census) and road tiles (gen_step_costs --roads), because both follow. Tune nothing to hit a count; if the rule as written leaves density far from the doc's shape, report and stop for Ben.

A WORLD-MOVER AND A SIM BEAT: a named cause in the sprint's one re-bless, measured in its own worktree. DONE WHEN the rule runs, POPULATION.md states it (done at the ruling), the per-seed centre count and land share are recorded old -> new, and the densest seed's road lens shows land that is not street.

Measure with stockpile_budget_check --firm-census before and after: the province_cap share of the budget, firms by the scale of the centre they stand in, budget firms against the 120 body ceiling, specialists chartered, markets.

RE-READ AFTER BL-1141 (2026-09-26, main 8cbdbc9d, stockpile_budget_check --firm-census): province_cap now binds on 16 of 16 worlds, 60.8M points pooled (5.2% of the budget, up from 1.0%), 181 bookings, about 756 firms' worth; largest 29.5% of a budget (seed 28, whose largest province is 1,383 tiles). Weighted by budget a window still spans 9-13 provinces. Unspent points are lost (charter_pool::none; nothing credits them). The larger loss is `remainder`, 63.7% of the pooled budget: most centres have under one firm price left after their specialist. The charter spend's window is ~49 tiles round each centre (stockpile_budget.cpp ~266-267): a large centre's window used to span 4-6 provinces (8-12 firms); now it sits inside one province, so after 2 firms every window tile is refused and the rest is booked unspent[province_cap] or never placed. THE WORK, measure only: firms placed and unspent by reason (province_cap above all) per seed on the 16 curated seeds, at 5cab560b^1 (before BL-1133) and at main; re-read after BL-1141. Then Ben rules on the cap (NR-910 was his). A named cause in the re-bless if it moves.

items.title: Empires earn naval points at sea, and carry them into the Exploration age as a starting fleet
items.design:
SETTLED (Ben, 2026-09-26, the naval carry-over form), written into EXPLORATION.md § the stocks (superseding the 2026-09-11 "the navy is new and starts at zero, everywhere"). A polity accrues NAVAL POINTS through the Empires span from three deeds: coastal provinces held, counted per year held (a held region with a port window, the empire tree's coastal_holdings reading); sea crossings made (the sea legs it walks); and coastal sea techs taken (EM-RD-2b Deep-Hull Sail, EM-RD-3b Lateen & Long-Range Rig, EM-RD-4a Ocean-Rated Hulls). At the handoff its points become its opening navy_stock. THE POINTS PASS TO THE POLITY THAT EARNED THEM: a polity that lost its coast keeps its sailors; nothing is read off the regions held at the handoff. The fleet is then an ordinary stock: upkeep from the first round, decay when underfunded, staged from a port; port_q stays endowment and no port carries.

EVIDENCE FOR IT (the sea lane, 2026-09-26): purchase-written lanes at 1960 are 0 of 444 on the 16 seeds (campaign 118, tribute 29, trade 297), consistent with a sea the Exploration age starts empty.

THE WORK, measure first: (1) today's first-crossing years, purchases and navy_stock by 1300 per seed; (2) the points ledger (the three deeds' shares per polity at 1200) and its conservation across the handoff (the cursor must carry it; world_cursor_equivalence folds it); (3) the conversion constant (points -> navy_stock) read on a ladder over the 16 seeds, reporting the opening fleets, the Exploration counters (crossings, purchases, subjections, battles, lanes by writer) at each rung; Ben picks the rung. Readings to name for Ben, not take silently: what a polity that dies before 1200 carries (nothing, as the ruling reads); how the three deeds are weighted against each other. A world-mover: a named cause in the re-bless. RUNS AFTER BL-1142 (far pairs across water) merges, in the sea lane.

items.design:
RULED (Ben, 2026-10-03): the Road cliff is accepted as the rule -- a tied pre-industrial block keeps its midpoint rank, and where it falls under 0.40 its roads stay Track. Haulage read before merge.

RULED (Ben, 2026-10-03): qualification reads the polity's own industrial crossing year (q.industrial_year) on a generated world; measured first. POPULATION.md § Qualification.

MEASURED (2026-10-03, 5aa6b7a9 + ea03e90e merged): shipped worlds carry Highway tiles only from the ancient-corridor works rule; the national rule qualifies 0 links on all 16 seeds, because every nation's qualification reads region::industrialised, which a generated world never sets (history_sim.cpp ~9080), so all tie at 0.05 (percentile 0.5, the all-tied shape). 13-37 nations a seed hold two or more City+; 35-179 City-City links laid. It builds no_prehistory worlds, which run no industrial urbanisation, so a nation holds at most one City+ and a Highway (two City+ centres in one nation) never qualifies. The shipped worlds now carry ~2,700 cities pooled (BL-1137 at x4 jobs), so they may well carry Highways. WORK: read Highway tiles and City-City links per curated seed on the shipped path; move R2 to (or add) a shipped-world reading; if shipped worlds still lay no Highway, report why for Ben. Never weaken R2 to pass.

items.title: What a good is worth wanting changes with the age, so industrial realms invade for coal and iron
items.design: SETTLED (Ben, 2026-10-03): EXPLORATION.md § A want ranks a campaign, "what a good is worth wanting changes with the age". TODAY: the campaign prize leans by w_want_q (1000) x the decider's want for the target's dominant good (BL-953); the want is the seat market's scarcity -- flat for every good, 300 if the realm holds it somewhere, 700 if nowhere, plus a population term (history_sim.cpp ~823-846) -- times the culture preference. Industrialisation inherits it unchanged, so coal is no more wanted in 1900 than grain in 1300. BUILD: a per-age weight table per good (farm, ore, energy, port) scaling scarcity_raw_q (or the want), one row per span (Exploration identity, Industrialisation with energy and ore up); read on a ladder over the 16 seeds (campaign targets by dominant good, conquests of energy/ore regions, battles, subjections), Ben sets the weights. Not a new AI grant: it leans an existing input (same idiom as w_want_q). Sprint 49.

items.design: FOUND 2026-10-03 (the BL-1145 cold review): NR-412 says province id 0 is a real province and no seam may use 0 as a sentinel, yet the battle glyph (body_surface_canvas.cpp ~3818 pid != 0), unit markers (~3850 prov_id != 0, the upid == 0 skip), the capital garrison seeding (nation_generation.cpp ~1561 cap_prov != 0) and battle discovery (battle_system.cpp ~494 prov == 0) all treat 0 as "no province". So province 0 never shows a marker, never gets a capital garrison, and never hosts a discovered battle. items.author: Ben (2026-10-03, the culture ground form note); filed by Claude
items.title: Amenities and the goods people consume through the ages, distinct from commercial products, carry a culture's preference
items.design: BEN'S NOTE (2026-10-03, keeping BL-1107's mapping for now): "I was considering amenities and goods that people consume through ages, rather than more commercial products." Today a cultural preference weights only the four abstract goods (farm, ore, energy, port), so a cradle's amenity must map onto a commercial good (forest -> energy). The idea: a small set of consumed amenity goods -- the things a people eats, drinks, wears and burns across the ages -- that preference attaches to, distinct from the industrial goods. DESIGN FIRST (a design session with Ben): which goods, how they map to TILES.md amenity classes, how they enter the want and trade, and how they hand over to the campaign's named resources. Not built until designed.
